subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real function √(16 − x²).

mark_split.label: Condition for the function to be defined

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.81 — VSAQ chapter 14 Functions, question 94.2, on ★★★ SSP 81 (the book calls it 'the most dominating domain page'). Appearance years are printed board-split. UNLIKE the LAQ and SAQ pages, the book prints NO internal mark split on its VSAQ pages: the 1+1 across the two steps is our division of the 2 marks, not the source's. Publisher's claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them. The only appearance printed for this one is 'IPE 09' — a pre-bifurcation paper (before the 2014 TS/AP split), for which appearances[].board has no value, so it is recorded here in prose rather than as data.

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the condition the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write the condition
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the condition alone. Write it before any factorising.

recall.must_convey: That the inside of the square root must be greater than or equal to zero: 16 − x² ≥ 0.
accept: sixteen minus x squared must be greater than or equal to zero
the inside of the root is non negative
set sixteen minus x squared at least zero
root lo unnadi non negative undali
the expression under the square root cannot be negative

steps.why: The same rule as every square root: the inside cannot be negative, so it alone fixes the domain.
common_mistakes: Reading the inequality the wrong way and taking the outside interval.
Forgetting to move x² across, so the factors come out wrong.

steps.label: Write the domain
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the interval itself. Write it in interval form, and check every bracket.

recall.must_convey: That the answer is the closed interval from minus 4 to 4, both endpoints included.
accept: the domain is minus four to four with both included
closed interval minus four comma four
x between minus four and four inclusive
domain is the closed interval minus 4 to 4

steps.why: Because equality is allowed at 16 − x² = 0, x = ±4 belong to the domain, so the brackets are square.
common_mistakes: Writing (−4, 4) and losing the two endpoints.
Giving the answer as a union, which is the solution to the opposite inequality.
